ut_summit_wall.blurb: Summit Wall is the tallest piece of rock in Lone Peak Cirque, high in the Central Wasatch above the Salt Lake valley. It holds about ten alpine-style trad lines on a mix of steep faces, cracks and roofs, with grades running from easy fifth class up to 5.12 and the bulk of them around 5.10. Every route starts from a pine-dotted shelf reached by climbing a snowfield or scree toward a big chimney, so early in the season expect snow on the way in. Helmets make sense here, since loose rock can fall and hikers topping out above can knock stones down. It is a committed, high-elevation objective.

ut_super_slab.blurb: Super Slab is the big, low-angle slab on the right as you drive into Little Cottonwood Canyon, reached from the Temple Quarry trail near the canyon mouth. It offers long routes by canyon standards, mostly trad with a couple of bolted lines and one short winter ice flow at an easy WI2 grade. Most climbing is moderate, from about 5.7 to 5.10 with a few harder lines, and the polished lower slabs reward good friction. Summer brings almost no shade, so spring and fall are the favored seasons. Rockfall is a concern, and runoff crosses the slab in spring.

ut_upper_fin.blurb: Upper Fin is the highest tier of The Fin, a buttress in Little Cottonwood Canyon in the Wasatch. It is a trad-only wall of about ten multi-pitch lines that run from 5.10 up to 5.12, so it suits experienced leaders. The climbing is slab and face work that has a reputation for being among the best in the canyon, and the lines are described as exposed and sparsely protected. Getting there means a steep, loose gully above the lower tiers with some route-finding through boulders and scrub oak.

ut_warrior_wall.blurb: Warrior Wall is a section of the Ruth Lake cliffs high in the Uinta Mountains, around 10,600 feet. It is a steep sport wall of about ten routes, nearly all between 5.10 and 5.12 with one trad line, so it is aimed at climbers already leading in the double digits. The wall sits back from its neighbors, a short scramble up talus from the cliff-base trail, and tends to be the least crowded spot at Ruth Lake. The cliffs here are mainly shady, which makes them a welcome escape on hot days.

ut_zen_garden.blurb: Zen Garden is a compact sport crag in the Right Fork of Maple Canyon in central Utah, on the canyon's typical conglomerate. The routes are all bolted and sit mostly in the 5.9 and 5.10 range with one 5.11, which makes it one of the friendlier places to start a day in a canyon known for harder climbing. It stays in shade early, so it works well as a morning warm-up. A short walk on the Pipe Dream Cave trail from the restroom leads to it.

ut_main_slab.blurb: Main Slab is the large, lower-angle slab you meet first on reaching the talus field at Geezer Wall in Big Cottonwood Canyon. About ten routes share it, mostly bolted sport lines with a few trad options, and every grade falls between roughly 5.5 and 5.7, so it is an approachable place for newer leaders. Climbs are described as fun, and some are longer and more exposed than you would expect. Falls are best avoided because of the gentle angle, and the talus below is unstable. In summer the wall is shaded until about noon, then sunny into the late afternoon.
